# Modifier-Primacy Status - Repository vs. Specification

**What this document is:** a from-scratch audit of how far the current repository (`d:\Utilities\XAMPP\htdocs\dndchar`) is from `docs/architecture/modifier-primacy.md`, generated by checking each rule in that specification directly against the schema, service layer, types, and UI. Where the spec and this document disagree about what the target model *should be*, the spec wins - this document only reports distance to that target.

**Methodology:** checked against migrations 001-019, `src/lib/server/services/*`, `src/lib/types/*`, `src/lib/rules/dnd5e.ts`, and the admin/character UI. This is a full regeneration, not an edit of any prior version.

---

## 0. Things to flag before the findings

**Spec claims that assume something not true of the codebase:**
- §2.1 and the Open Questions list both refer to **Soulfire** and **Vowfire** as existing resource pools. Neither exists anywhere in code - no `modifier_targets` row, no resource table, no string literal. They are aspirational only.
- §5.2's worked example talks about "Rage (the class feature)" and "Raging (the state)" as two distinct things. The actual seed data has exactly one `Rage` row with its modifiers attached directly - there is no `Raging` entity. This implies content needs to be re-modeled as two pieces, not only that the engine needs a new capability.
- §3.1's stacking table states the count-based advantage pool rule as confirmed. The current code implements standard 5e's binary cancellation rule - a real, behavioural divergence (see §4).

---

## 1. Fully Conforms

Rules where the live code already does what the spec requires.

- **§2.1 - Modifier definition carries no duration, cost, or instance-source.** `modifier_definitions` holds only `target`, `modifier_type`, `default_value_expression`, `label`, `description`. Duration and cost live on the Container side.
- **§2.1 - Dot-notation target convention.** Confirmed throughout seed data and `modifier_targets`: `ability_check.str`, `attack_roll.all`, `damage_taken.bludgeoning`, etc.
- **§2.1 - Fixed and Dice value sources.** `default_value_expression` stores literal numbers and dice expressions; both are consumed correctly by the roll/bonus resolution code.
- **§2.2 - Empty-grant Containers (mundane inventory).** `character_inventory_items.source_content_id` is nullable, and freeform items are fully insertable with no mechanics attached.
- **§2.4 - Duration/lifecycle excluded from the Modifier.** `duration_type`, `duration_rounds`, `requires_concentration`, `expiry_boundary` all live on `content_definitions` (as of migration 019), never on `modifier_definitions`.
- **§3.1 - Flat numeric add/subtract sums normally.** `resolvedNumericModifiers` flat-maps every matching modifier's resolved value and sums them with no special-casing.
- **§4.2 - Mechanics always resolve against the live definition.** `resolveCharacterModifierSources` queries `modifier_definitions` directly every time; no mechanic text is frozen in snapshots.
- **§4.3 - Soft-delete only.** `is_archived` exists on `modifier_targets`, `modifier_definitions`, and `content_definitions`. No service code hard-deletes a definition row.
- **§4.5 - Update-in-place vs. fork-a-copy.** Both paths are real: `update` is gated behind a `confirmShared` checkbox server-side; `copy` forks a new independent definition.
- **§6.1 - Three-tier permission split.** `requireAdmin` in `hooks.server.ts` gates the `/admin` route prefix. `isAdmin` prop from `data.user?.role === 'admin'` gates all mechanical-authoring UI in the character sheet (Quick Add modal, Create Homebrew link, modifier attachment forms).
- **§6.2 - Authoring and applying separated in UI.** The Catalogue tab has been removed from the player-facing character sheet tab set. Catalogue browsing and authoring live exclusively in dedicated admin screens.
- **§6.3 - A Container may attach multiple independent Modifier instances.** `ContentTypeAdmin.svelte`'s repeatable `?/attachModifier` form adds one `content_modifier_links` row per submission; nothing limits a content record to a single modifier.
- **§6.4 - Two-phase roll resolution for outcome-dependent conditions.** Attack roll phase runs first; crit detection gates damage modifier conditions before the damage roll is computed.

---

## 2. Partially Conforms (Needs Reshaping)

Rules where a real, working piece of the mechanism exists, but it is incomplete or scoped too narrowly.

- **§2.1 - Modifier target categories.** Derived stats, roll categories, and discrete rules are all real and seeded. Resource-pool targets are conceptually supported by dot-notation but no actual `resource.*` targets exist yet - Soulfire/Vowfire have zero representation. Needs extending.
- **§2.1 - Stat-derived formula value source.** `modifier_targets.value_kind` declares a `formula` kind, but `resolveModifierNumericValue` (`dnd5e.ts`) only evaluates one hardcoded literal (`rage_damage_bonus`). No general formula evaluator exists.
- **§2.2 - Container field completeness.** Migration 019 added `activation_type`, `cost_json`, `duration_type`, `duration_rounds`, `requires_concentration`, `expiry_boundary`, `stack_behavior` to `content_definitions`. These fields are present but the **service layer** (catalogue.ts, characters.ts) does not yet read or honour `cost_json` or `activation_type` declaratively - cost is still handled procedurally per content type. The schema is right; the engine hasn't caught up.
- **§2.3 - Structured cost list.** `cost_json JSONB` now exists on `content_definitions`. No engine path reads it yet to deduct multi-pool costs at activation time.
- **§2.5 - Source and target-of-effect tracked independently.** The schema is ready (`active_character_effects.source_character_id` exists). No UI and no service code actually exercises cross-character targeting.
- **§2.6 - Audit trail for every resolved value.** Real and working for attack rolls and damage (`rollDamageExpression` builds a labelled breakdown). AC, skill checks, saving throws have `?` formula modals with source attribution. Not uniformly structured as a reusable audit-trail type - each value implements its own breakdown independently.
- **§3.1 - Advantage/disadvantage - per-bucket scoping.** `resolveAdvantageState` does collect matching modifiers per target list and can be called with a scoped candidate list. The count-based pool is now wired (`resolveDicePool`). However, the **cancellation rule** remains a direct conflict - see §4.
- **§5.1 - Containers granting Containers.** `content_grants` exists and is joined in `resolveCharacterModifierSources` (branch 4). Migration 019 populates it with effect-as-Container grants from `content_effect_links`. One hop only - no recursive grant chain walking yet.

---

## 3. Missing Entirely

Rules with no trace anywhere in schema, services, or UI.

- **§2.1 - Derived-from-sibling value source.** No column, no resolver branch. Crit-bonus damage derived from a weapon's own base die doesn't exist in any form.
- **§2.3 - Cost engine.** The `cost_json` column exists but nothing reads it to deduct resources at activation time. The cost of casting/activating anything is still hard-coded procedurally in service functions.
- **§2.4 - Expiry side-effects as a grant-on-trigger.** No `on_expire` trigger type. A Container that fires something specific when it wears off (spec's Haste-lethargy example) has no mechanism.
- **§3.1 - Resistance/vulnerability per-damage-type netting.** No code nets resistance against vulnerability per damage type.
- **§3.1 - "Doesn't stack with itself" flag.** No per-modifier-definition boolean for this. The adjacent `effect_definitions.stack_behavior` enum controls re-application behaviour, not modifier-level stacking exceptions.
- **§3.1 - Resource-grant-sums-by-count.** Nothing resembling countable resource grants that sum across sources (the `luck_dice` pattern) exists. `character_content_resources` tracks a single current/max value per definition.
- **§4.4 - Version-history drift display.** `VersionList.svelte` renders a label and a restore button only. No logic distinguishes character-state diffs from modifier-definition drift. No drift display at all.
- **Magic system - concentration state tracking.** `spell_definitions.concentration` is a boolean metadata field only. No mechanism enforces the "only one concentration spell at a time" rule or applies the concentration Container to the character when a spell is cast.
- **Magic system - cost engine for spell slots.** Spell slots are deducted procedurally in `castCharacterSpell`. They are not declared as `cost_json` on the spell Container and not handled by a general cost engine.

---

## 4. Direct Conflicts

Rules where the current code actively does something different from what the spec requires.

- **§2.2 - Unified Container concept - in progress (migration 019).** The live schema now has `content_definitions` extended with Container-level fields, and `effect_definitions` and `action_definitions` have been migrated into `content_definitions` as `content_type = 'condition'` and `content_type = 'action'` respectively. The rule engine's branch 1 (previously `effect_definitions → effect_modifier_links`) now routes through `container_id → content_definitions → content_modifier_links` for all active character effects. **The old tables (`effect_definitions`, `action_definitions`, `content_effect_links`) are preserved for now as read-only legacy.** Service-layer code (`catalogue.ts`, `characters.ts`, `effects.ts`) still writes to the old tables - updating these services to write to `content_definitions` directly is the remaining work for this conflict.

- **§3.1 - Advantage/disadvantage cancellation rule.** The spec requires count-based pool netting (2 adv + 1 disadv = net +1, roll 2 dice take highest). `resolveAdvantageState` (`dnd5e.ts`) currently returns `'normal'` whenever any opposing source exists, which is the standard 5e binary cancellation rule. The count-based pool mechanic exists in `resolveDicePool` but `resolveAdvantageState` does not call it - the two functions are not yet wired together in the roll resolution path.

## 5. Magic System - Design Requirements

The magic system is the largest single feature gap from a player-experience standpoint. It overlaps significantly with the Container unification (spells are Containers) and the cost engine (spell slot costs are structured costs). This section documents the design requirements so they can be implemented alongside the Container work.

### 5.1 What the spec says about spells

Spells are Containers. There is no special "Spell" entity type in the architecture - a spell is a named Container with an `activation_type` of `active_use`, `cost_json` that declares its slot level and amount, and optional grants (Containers or Modifiers that activate while the spell is in effect). This is the same shape as a class feature, a feat, or a condition - only the metadata differs.

### 5.2 Spell-specific metadata (retained from `spell_definitions`)

These fields are spell-flavour metadata, not new mechanical concepts:
- `spell_level` (0-9) - determines minimum slot level
- `school` - flavour only
- `casting_time` - action economy source: maps to `cost_json` pool `action`, `bonus_action`, or `reaction`
- `range`, `components`, `duration`, `ritual`, `higher_level` - flavour/reference only
- `concentration` - determines whether the Container sets `requires_concentration = true`; enforced by the cost engine when the spell is cast
- `classes` - determines who can learn it

### 5.3 What needs designing (currently open)

**Concentration enforcement:** When a concentration spell is activated, any previously active Container with `requires_concentration = true` on the same character must be deactivated. This is a rule in the cost/activation engine, not in the Container definition itself.

**Upcasting:** A spell may be cast at a higher slot level than its minimum. The cast-level choice changes the `cost_json` amount deducted. The spell's `higher_level` text describes the upcast benefit; the mechanical expression of that benefit (extra damage dice, extended duration, etc.) is currently only text - it needs to be Modifier instances gated on `condition_expression: 'cast_level >= N'`.

**Ritual casting:** An alternate activation path with no slot cost but a +10-minute casting time. Not representable as `cost_json = []` alone (zero cost spells currently have no way to declare the time cost). A `ritual: true` flag on the spell Container's metadata plus an alternate activation path in the engine.

**Cantrips (level 0):** `spell_level = 0`, `cost_json = []` (no slot). Cantrip damage scaling by level (the 5e rule where cantrips deal more damage at character level 5/11/17) is a Modifier gated on a character-level condition - currently not expressible because no condition type for "character total level >= N" exists in `modifierConditionMatches`.

**Prepared vs. known spells:** Wizards prepare from a known list; Warlocks know and always have prepared; Clerics/Druids have always-prepared domain spells plus a daily preparation. The `is_known` / `is_prepared` flags on `character_content_instances` already exist; the preparation rules per class are not enforced anywhere and need explicit per-class logic.

**Spell attack rolls:** `content_definitions` rows for spells that require an attack roll need a Modifier instance on `spell_attack_roll` (type `bonus`, value `proficiency_bonus + spellcasting_ability_modifier`). This is already expressible; the existing seed data may be incomplete.

### 5.4 Spell slots - current state vs. target

Current: `character_spell_slots` (separate table), decremented directly in `castCharacterSpell`.

Target: Spell slots are just character resource pools - `character_resources` entries with `resource_key = 'spell_slot_1'` through `spell_slot_9`, plus `pact_slot_1`-`pact_slot_9` for Warlocks. The cost engine reads `cost_json` from the spell Container and deducts from the matching pool. `character_spell_slots` becomes legacy once this migration is complete.

This is a significant migration (removing a dedicated table, replacing with generic resource pools) and should be treated as a separate task after the cost engine is in place.

## 6. Container Unification - Current Progress and Remaining Work

### 6.1 What migration 019 accomplished

- `content_definitions` now carries all Container-level fields: `activation_type`, `cost_json`, `duration_type`, `duration_rounds`, `requires_concentration`, `expiry_boundary`, `stack_behavior`, `is_system`.
- `content_type` now accepts `'condition'` and `'action'` in addition to the original four.
- All rows from `effect_definitions` were inserted into `content_definitions` with `content_type = 'condition'` (key prefix `condition:`).
- All rows from `effect_modifier_links` were migrated into `content_modifier_links` for the new condition Containers.
- `active_character_effects` now has a `container_id` column referencing `content_definitions`. Existing rows were back-filled. New active effects should set `container_id` in addition to (or instead of) `effect_id`.
- All rows from `action_definitions` were inserted into `content_definitions` with `content_type = 'action'` (key prefix `action:`).
- `action_steps` and `content_action_links` now each have a `container_id` column referencing the new action Containers.
- `content_effect_links` rows were migrated into `content_grants` (effect grants become Container grants).
- The rule engine (`resolveCharacterModifierSources`) branch 1 now queries via `container_id → content_definitions → content_modifier_links`, with a legacy fallback for any remaining rows where `container_id IS NULL`.

### 6.2 Remaining service-layer work

The following service functions still write to the old tables and need updating to write to `content_definitions` directly:

| Function | File | Old write target | New target |
|---|---|---|---|
| `applyCharacterEffect` | `effects.ts` | `active_character_effects.effect_id` | `active_character_effects.container_id` |
| `removeCharacterEffect` | `effects.ts` | looks up by `effect_id` | look up by `container_id` |
| `listEffectDefinitions` | `characters.ts` | `effect_definitions` query | `content_definitions WHERE content_type = 'condition'` |
| `getActiveEffects` | `characters.ts` | UNION through `effect_definitions` | UNION through `content_definitions` via `container_id` |
| `createHomebrewContent` | `catalogue.ts` | routes on old `ContentType` | add 'condition' and 'action' routing |
| `executeActionStep` | `catalogue.ts` | `action_steps.action_id` | `action_steps.container_id` |
| `triggerCharacterContentActions` | `catalogue.ts` | `content_action_links.action_id` | `content_action_links.action_container_id` |

### 6.3 Tables that can be dropped after service-layer migration is complete

- `effect_definitions` (superseded by `content_definitions WHERE content_type = 'condition'`)
- `effect_modifier_links` (superseded by `content_modifier_links` on condition Containers)
- `active_character_effects.effect_id` column (superseded by `container_id`)
- `content_effect_links` (superseded by `content_grants`)
- `action_definitions` (superseded by `content_definitions WHERE content_type = 'action'`)
- `action_steps.action_id` column (superseded by `container_id`)
- `content_action_links.action_id` column (superseded by `action_container_id`)

Do not drop these until all write paths above are confirmed updated and tested.

## 7. What changed since the prior version of this document

- **§6.1 Permission tiers** - moved from §3 Missing Entirely to §1 Fully Conforms. `requireAdmin` guards `/admin` routes; `isAdmin` prop gates all mechanical-authoring UI.
- **§6.2 Catalogue tab separation** - moved from §4 Direct Conflicts to §1 Fully Conforms. The Catalogue tab no longer appears on the player-facing character sheet.
- **§6.4 Two-phase roll resolution** - moved from §3 Missing Entirely to §1 Fully Conforms.
- **§2.2 Container unification** - status changed from "Direct Conflict - not started" to "Direct Conflict - in progress." Migration 019 ran; schema extended; rule engine branch 1 updated. Service-layer migration is the remaining work.
- **Hit dice management** - per-class hit dice pools (`hit_dice_0`, `hit_dice_1`, ...) added to `character_resources`, tracked via index-based keys to avoid class name conflicts. `spendHitDice` action and `useHitDie` client function implement HP recovery with CON modifier and headroom capping. Short/long rest restoration of hit dice pools is deferred (see §3 pending items).
- **Formula audit modals** - `?` help buttons on all derived values (AC, proficiency, saves, skills, initiative, speed, spell DC, spell attack) open a modal showing source-attributed breakdown. Not yet a unified audit-trail type, but uniformly present.
